operations.evidence: True, false and null outcome-linked-to-search states were preserved.
Null was not converted to false and the field was not treated as a general effectiveness measure.
The 64-character crime key required for outcome history and the returned crime-plus-outcomes structure were recorded.
The API key was not represented as a police case number or proof of spatial accuracy.
The explicit unavailability of crime outcomes for PSNI through this method was recorded.
Endpoint unavailability was not converted to a zero outcome or generalized to England and Wales.
Optional suspect or offender person_id semantics were recorded.
Missing person_id was not treated as proof that no person was involved or exposed as a public identity.
Internal outcome codes and human-readable names were preserved separately.
Display names were not substituted for stable codes and codes were not treated as ordered severity.
Outcome date and crime month were preserved as separate temporal fields.
Outcome date did not overwrite crime month and elapsed time remained an explicit calculation.
Specific-location, point-radius and custom-polygon outcome query modes were recorded.
Results from spatially different query modes were not silently pooled.
The 10,000-outcome custom-area ceiling and HTTP 503 response were recorded.
A 503 from an oversized area was not misclassified as general service absence.
Colon-separated polygon vertices and implicit straight-line closure were recorded.
Implicit closure was not assumed geometrically harmless and polygon validity remained caller-controlled.
Latitude-longitude requests resolving to the nearest predefined crime location were recorded.
Nearest-location results were not represented as exact-point or parcel-specific crime.
Force and BTP location_type values were recorded as provenance fields.
Location type was not treated as an offence category or exact-coordinate guarantee.
BTP locations overlapping territorial-force boundaries were recorded.
Spatial overlap was not treated as duplicate proof without record-level identifiers.
BTP-specific location_subtype semantics were recorded separately from location_type.
Empty subtype was not generalized as a missing-crime signal or assigned to territorial records.
Latest outcome category and its date were preserved as a pair.
Latest status was not represented as complete case history and missing status was not treated as no investigation.
The official open-data page's 23 April 2026 update and refreshed product set were recorded.
Page update date was not substituted for every table's observation period.
The separate recorded-crime geographical reference table was recorded as a supporting asset.
Reference geography was not treated as parcel geometry and joins remain edition-dependent.
The separate recorded-crime offence reference table was recorded.
Offence reference labels were not converted into risk weights and edition changes remain possible.
The national Home Office standard for recording and counting notifiable offences in England and Wales was recorded.
A national standard was not treated as proof of identical local implementation or parcel safety.
PEEL effectiveness, efficiency and legitimacy coverage of all 43 England and Wales forces was recorded.
Force inspection judgments were not represented as parcel observations and report dates remain force-specific.
Adaptive cycle questions and the distinct 2025-2027 PEEL methodology were recorded.
Grades from different cycles were not compared without framework context or converted into safety scores.
Rows 431-450 were published as official-source roles with explicit endpoint, edition and scope limitations; no candidate value was derived.

All 12 candidates remain unjoined at confidence zero; source rows 411-450 and operation rows 1015-1098 were published without a second runner, task, candidate value, business row, database write, migration or deployment.
